chapter: South Side scene and Bunk Johnson
title: Wartime jazz concerts at Moose Hall and Orchestra Hall
summary: Rinker vaguely recalls jazz concerts after he left the army, sponsored by Catherine Jacobson, where he played with the Burt Kelly Stables band.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: the Moose Hall. It was after I came out of the army and I don't remember if Bunk was there that day or not. He may have been. I know Baby Dot was there and we played together that day. Uh Bud Freeman was there. Tut's Oper. Well I can't remember who all was there. What year did that mean? Uh 1945 or 46. It was supposed to be a jazz concert for me but it was all mixed up. We we shared honors equally pretty much. I have a vague recollection of being a participant in a jazz concert during the war years. It was probably 19 I was I was home in uniform and it was at Orchestra Hall and I think there were two of them on successive Sundays and I was there both times. I played a little I think. I can't remember it. It's been so long ago but Catherine Jacobson could tell you all about it. I think she sponsored the things and they were very well attended. The recollection is very vague. I think Fats Waller was there. Pretty sure. I know that the Burt Kelly Stables Band was there and it seems to me that I played a set with the Stables Band and played some Natty Dominic that day. Oh. But it uh it's begging my mind. Catherine Jacobson could fill you in on the whole thing if you can reach her. Get in touch with her. She's in Florida. I think.
